findings.title: Untrusted Input Sanitization and Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: Input from external sources is processed without strict sanitization, allowing SQL, Command, or Template Injection.
findings.mitigation: Implement strict input validation schemas, parameterized SQL queries, and context-aware output encoding.

findings.title: Missing Input Bounds and Memory Safety Checks
findings.description: Memory manipulation or payload processing lacks boundary checking, creating buffer overflow or payload mutation risks.
findings.mitigation: Use memory-safe languages or enforce strict length and boundary checks on all inbound buffers and payloads.

findings.title: Insecure Object Deserialization
findings.description: Process deserializes untrusted data using unsafe deserializers (such as pickle or unsafe YAML loaders), allowing adversaries to alter internal execution graphs and execute arbitrary code.
findings.mitigation: Use safe data-only serialization formats (JSON, Protobuf) or strictly enforce safe loaders (e.g. yaml.safe_load) without arbitrary class instantiation.

findings.title: Missing Security Audit Logging
findings.description: Critical business transactions and security state transitions occur without generating audit trails, allowing actors to repudiate actions.
findings.mitigation: Implement non-repudiable audit logging for sensitive operations including identity, timestamp, action, and outcome.

findings.title: Verbose Error Details and Stack Trace Disclosure
findings.description: Process does not mask internal runtime exceptions, exposing stack traces, framework versions, and database schemas in error responses.
findings.mitigation: Implement centralized error-handling middleware that returns generic error messages to clients while logging stack traces internally.

findings.title: Insecure Secrets Management and Credential Exposure
findings.description: Secrets, database credentials, or private keys are not managed via dedicated secrets vaults, risking exposure via source code, logs, or environment dumping.
findings.mitigation: Use dedicated secrets managers (HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) and avoid storing credentials in plain environment variables.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability
findings.description: Process fetches remote resources based on user-supplied URLs without restricting target IP addresses, enabling internal cloud metadata probing.
findings.mitigation: Validate and whitelist target URLs, disable HTTP redirects on outbound clients, and block private IP address ranges (RFC 1918, link-local 169.254.169.254).

findings.title: Path Traversal and Arbitrary File Disclosure
findings.description: Process resolves file system paths using untrusted user input without canonicalization, enabling directory traversal to read arbitrary system files or application code.
findings.mitigation: Validate input against an allowlist, use canonical path resolution (e.g., Path.resolve()), and verify paths stay within authorized base directories.

findings.title: Missing Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)
findings.description: Process executes with elevated operating system or cluster privileges, allowing an attacker who breaches it to compromise the entire host.
findings.mitigation: Run processes as dedicated unprivileged system users, drop root capabilities, and apply container security profiles.

findings.title: Missing Authorization and Role-Based Access Control
findings.description: Operations and routes lack role-based authorization checks, allowing authenticated low-privilege users to access administrative features.
findings.mitigation: Enforce strict server-side authorization checks on every operation (Broken Object Level Authorization - BOLA prevention).

findings.title: Unrestricted System Command Execution
findings.description: Process retains the ability to spawn subshells or run arbitrary system commands, opening doors to privilege escalation via shell escapes.
findings.mitigation: Avoid invoking shell commands; use native programming libraries and restrict command execution via sandboxing or seccomp.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Process or API Endpoint
findings.description: Endpoints or processes without enforced authentication allow untrusted adversaries to forge requests and impersonate legitimate clients.
findings.mitigation: Enforce strong authentication mechanisms (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT or API Keys) before executing business logic.

findings.title: Weak or Unvalidated Session Identifiers
findings.description: The process does not properly validate or rotate session identifiers, leaving it susceptible to session hijacking or fixation.
findings.mitigation: Use cryptographically random session tokens, invalidate them on logout, and bind them securely to client context.

findings.title: Unvalidated Redirection Target (Open Redirect)
findings.description: Process performs HTTP redirects using user-supplied parameters without validation, facilitating phishing and credential theft.
findings.mitigation: Maintain an explicit whitelist of allowed redirect URLs and validate targets strictly before initiating redirection.

findings.title: Overly Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)
findings.description: Process configures wildcard origins or insecure CORS policies alongside credentials, allowing malicious external domains to impersonate authenticated browser clients.
findings.mitigation: Restrict allowed origins to an explicit trusted domain whitelist and disallow wildcard origins when credentials are supported.

findings.title: Unauthorized Datastore Modification
findings.description: The datastore does not enforce strict access control or integrity verification on write operations, risking record tampering.
findings.mitigation: Configure strict database permissions, access control lists (ACLs), and row-level security.

findings.title: Mutable or Tamperable Audit Log Storage
findings.description: Logs or audit stores can be modified or deleted by privileged or compromised processes, undermining accountability.
findings.mitigation: Send logs to write-once-read-many (WORM) storage, centralized append-only log services, or use cryptographic log chaining.

findings.title: Unencrypted Sensitive Data at Rest
findings.description: The datastore does not enforce encryption at rest, exposing records if storage media, backups, or underlying instances are compromised.
findings.mitigation: Enable storage volume encryption (AES-256) and field-level encryption for high-sensitivity data.

findings.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information in Unmasked Storage
findings.description: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or credentials stored without data masking or tokenization risk exposure to unauthorized internal staff.
findings.mitigation: Implement pseudonymization, data masking, and tokenization for sensitive personal attributes.

findings.title: Datastore Capacity Exhaustion
findings.description: Datastores without data retention limits or volume quotas can be exhausted by continuous writes, crashing dependent applications.
findings.mitigation: Set disk quotas, automated retention policies, and monitoring alerts for storage capacity.

findings.title: Datastore Unavailability and Data Loss from Missing Backups
findings.description: Datastore lacks automated backups and multi-region replication, leading to permanent denial of service and data loss during hardware failure or ransomware.
findings.mitigation: Enable automated daily snapshots, point-in-time recovery (PITR), and cross-region replication for persistent data stores.

findings.title: Untrusted External Entity Impersonation
findings.description: External interactors operating outside the organization trust zone can forge identity or origin headers unless verified as a trusted party.
findings.mitigation: Authenticate external clients via mutual TLS, signed API keys, or identity provider verification, and establish trust boundaries.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Operations by External Entity
findings.description: External entity executes actions or sends data without mandatory authentication or signature, preventing non-repudiation and forensic tracing.
findings.mitigation: Enforce client identity authentication, cryptographic request signatures, and audit timestamps at entry gateways.

findings.description: External interactors operating outside the organization trust zone can forge identity or origin headers unless verified as a trusted party.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Operations by External Entity
findings.description: External entity executes actions or sends data without mandatory authentication or signature, preventing non-repudiation and forensic tracing.

findings.title: Unauthorized Datastore Modification
findings.description: The datastore does not enforce strict access control or integrity verification on write operations, risking record tampering.
findings.mitigation: Configure strict database permissions, access control lists (ACLs), and row-level security.

findings.title: Mutable or Tamperable Audit Log Storage
findings.description: Logs or audit stores can be modified or deleted by privileged or compromised processes, undermining accountability.
findings.mitigation: Send logs to write-once-read-many (WORM) storage, centralized append-only log services, or use cryptographic log chaining.

findings.title: Unencrypted Sensitive Data at Rest
findings.description: The datastore does not enforce encryption at rest, exposing records if storage media, backups, or underlying instances are compromised.

findings.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information in Unmasked Storage
findings.description: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or credentials stored without data masking or tokenization risk exposure to unauthorized internal staff.
findings.mitigation: Implement pseudonymization, data masking, and tokenization for sensitive personal attributes.

findings.title: Datastore Capacity Exhaustion
findings.description: Datastores without data retention limits or volume quotas can be exhausted by continuous writes, crashing dependent applications.
findings.mitigation: Set disk quotas, automated retention policies, and monitoring alerts for storage capacity.

findings.title: Datastore Unavailability and Data Loss from Missing Backups
findings.description: Datastore lacks automated backups and multi-region replication, leading to permanent denial of service and data loss during hardware failure or ransomware.
findings.mitigation: Enable automated daily snapshots, point-in-time recovery (PITR), and cross-region replication for persistent data stores.
